cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: CWE-93 specifically addresses CRLF sequence injection for protocol/format manipulation, not HTML attribute injection. The demonstrated vulnerability involves unquoted HTML attribute injection, not CRLF-based protocol injection.

connection.evidence: User-controlled title parameter from markdown input flows directly into unquoted HTML title attribute via string interpolation: `title=${title}`

diff_causality.evidence: If this line were reverted, the title attribute would not be rendered at all when title is null, preventing the injection vector. The addition creates the vulnerable code path.

security_control.required_control: CRLF sequence neutralization for protocol/format boundaries
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-93 requires controls specifically for CRLF sequence neutralization in protocol contexts
existing_controls_checked: No CRLF-specific validation observed in the code path
security_control.deficiency_evidence: The demonstrated issue is HTML attribute quoting deficiency, not CRLF injection. No evidence shows CRLF sequences being used as special elements or requiring neutralization.

concrete_impact.evidence: Unquoted attribute allows injection of additional HTML attributes and JavaScript via whitespace characters, enabling XSS in the Electron application context

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the title attribute would not be rendered when title is null, eliminating the unquoted attribute injection vector entirely.
supporting_evidence: User-controlled title parameter flows directly into unquoted HTML attribute
No validation or escaping applied to title parameter before HTML construction
contradicting_evidence: CWE-93 mechanism focuses on CRLF sequence injection for protocols/formats, not HTML attribute injection
No evidence of CRLF sequences being used as special separators in this context
unresolved_facts: Whether this.options.sanitize is enabled in practice
How marked.js normalizes title parameter parsing
